item.title: Resonance interaction of vector breathers and exotic dynamics in the coupled Hirota equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents a systematic theoretical investigation of vector breathers and their nonlinear interactions in the coupled Hirota equation. This model describes the simultaneous propagation of ultrashort optical pulses in optical fibers and contains a key parameter that characterizes the strength of higher-order linear and nonlinear effects, such as third-order dispersion and self-steepening. For the model, we focus on the focusing-focusing case. On a nonzero plane-wave background, we derive explicit expressions for multi-breather solutions of the coupled Hirota equation by the dressing method. For the single-breather solution, by choosing special constant vectors, the vector breathers can be classified into three fundamental types: Type I, Type II, and Type III. We then analyze their characteristic parameters, including spatial localization and group velocity, as well as important special cases such as the Kuznetsov-Ma breathers, Peregrine soliton, and Akhmediev type breathers etc. Through the above analysis, we find that the higher-order effect parameter only modifies the propagation velocity and oscillation period of the breathers, while the resonance conditions remain satisfied: when the wave numbers and frequencies match, inelastic resonant interactions can occur between Type I and Type II breathers, manifesting either as a fusion process (I + II \rightarrow II) or the reverse decay process (III \rightarrow I + II). Furthermore, we present the explicit expression for the two breather solutions of the equation and analyze its rich interaction scenarios, including two breather resonances and elastic collisions, and we point out that the special case of resonance corresponds to the limiting case of merging eigenvalues. Finally, we carry out numerical simulations to verify the accuracy of the obtained solutions.
item.dc:creator: Li-Juan Bo, Xiu-Bin Wang

item.title: Physics-Transfer Learning: A Physics-Constrained Theory for Zero-Shot Generalization Along the Ladder of Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2610.22376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable out-of-distribution generalization remains a central challenge in machine learning, particularly when models are deployed in data-scarce high-fidelity domains. Existing approaches often rely on statistical distribution alignment, or invariance assumptions that can fail when domain shifts reflect changes in underlying mechanisms. Inspired by a longstanding paradigm in physics that understands complex systems by starting from tractable idealizations and progressively incorporating additional mechanisms and levels of fidelity, we propose physics-transfer (PT) learning, a physics-constrained learning theory for zero-shot generalization along a ladder of complexity. PT constructs chains of anchor domains (CADs) that connect low-cost source domains to complex targets and introduces computable feasibility and reliability indicators for assessing transfer before target-domain labels are observed. Under physical-consistency and stable-representation assumptions, we derive an operational upper bound on target risk in terms of source empirical risk, the PT indicators, and finite-sample errors, and establish convergence as adjacent complexity gaps shrink and data coverage improves. We evaluate PT on excited-state energy prediction in quantum systems and dynamical-transition prediction in classical systems using neural networks trained without target-domain labels. Across substantial distribution shifts, PT yields accurate high-fidelity predictions, while the indicators identify incorrect physical mappings before target-domain prediction fails. These results provide a model-agnostic framework for designing, diagnosing, and controlling generalization in data-scarce learning problems.
item.dc:creator: Yingjie Zhao, Zhiping Xu

item.title: A generalized long-wave limit method with spectral perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2606.15174v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a generalized long-wave limit method for constructing higher-order (degenerate) lump solutions of $(2+1)$-dimensional integrable systems. Starting from the multi-soliton tau function, we introduce wavenumber rescalings, spectral perturbations, and higher-order phase modulations in a single small parameter, and choose their coefficients so that the lower-order Taylor coefficients vanish. Applying this framework to the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili I equation, we explicitly derive second-order two- and three-lump solutions as well as third-order three-, four-, five-, and six-lump solutions. The long-time asymptotics of the peak positions and amplitudes describe anomalous scattering of these degenerate lump solutions. Extensions to hybrid higher-order lump solutions associated with multiple distinct spectral parameters are also discussed.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Qiu, Zhen Wang

item.title: Blinking membrane patterns induced by protein binding/unbinding
item.description: arXiv:2608.13016v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nonequilibrium membrane pattern formation is studied using meshless membrane simulation. Bound proteins are considered to have two states that generate different membrane spontaneous curvatures. Protein binding and unbinding occur cyclically owing to chemical potential differences, as an off-lattice active Potts model. It is found that this cyclic binding/unbinding can induce blinking domains, with oscillating size: convex domains of the proteins with a higher spontaneous curvature grow, and subsequently, the proteins change to the other state with a lower spontaneous curvature, resulting in domain shrinkage. These processes repeat. In thermal equilibrium, hexagonal convex domains are formed by the competition between bending and surface tension energies, so that they are stably formed only under positive surface tension. However, blinking domains can form even in tensionless membranes.
item.dc:creator: Hiroshi Noguchi
